title: Split Array Into Maximum Number of Subarrays
summary: Given an array nums consisting of non-negative integers, split the array into one or more subarrays such that each element of the array belongs to exactly one subarray.
statement: Given an array nums consisting of non-negative integers, split the array into one or more subarrays such that each element of the array belongs to exactly one subarray. The goal is to minimize the sum of the bitwise AND scores of these subarrays. The bitwise AND score of a subarray nums[l..r] is calculated as nums[l] AND nums[l + 1] AND ... AND nums[r], where AND is the bitwise AND operation. Return the maximum number of subarrays that can be formed while satisfying these conditions.
constraints: nums is a nonempty array of nonnegative integers.
Partition all elements into contiguous nonempty subarrays and minimize the sum of each part’s bitwise-AND score.
Among minimum-score partitions, return the maximum number of parts.
hints: The smallest possible score sum is the AND of the entire array, and when that value is zero every optimal part can score zero.
Greedily cut whenever the running AND first becomes zero; if it never does, keep one part.
Reset the running AND after every zero segment and count the cuts.
AND can only lose bits as a segment grows, so the earliest zero cut preserves the most suffix opportunities; if total AND is nonzero, every extra positive-score part would increase the sum.
editorial: AND can only lose bits as a segment grows, so the earliest zero cut preserves the most suffix opportunities; if total AND is nonzero, every extra positive-score part would increase the sum.

tests.explanation: Three consecutive groups can each achieve AND zero, the global minimum sum.
The entire array AND is one; splitting would increase the minimum total score, so return one.
